sanskrit: yuyutsuḥ saṃjayaś caiva tat kartāsmy aham añjasā sarve hy ete 'numānyā me kulasyāsya hitaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Yuyutsu and Saṃjaya too — what they advise I shall do at once; for all of these are worthy of my regard, well-wishers of this our line.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu yāce nṛpate tvām ahaṃ śirasā nataḥ kriyatāṃ tāvad āhāras tato gacchāśramaṃ prati
english: But this one thing I beg of you, O king, my head bowed low: first let a meal be taken, and then set out for the hermitage.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājñābhyanujñāto dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pratāpavān yayau svabhavanaṃ rājā gāndhāryānugatas tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, with the king's leave, the majestic Dhṛtarāṣṭra went to his own dwelling, followed by Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: mandaprāṇagatir dhīmān kṛcchrād iva samuddharan padātiḥ sa mahīpālo jīrṇo gajapatir yathā
english: Slow of breath and step, the wise lord of the earth went on foot, hauling himself along as if with effort, like an aged lordly elephant.

sanskrit: tam anvagacchad viduro vidvān sūtaś ca saṃjayaḥ sa cāpi parameṣvāsaḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tathā
english: Behind him walked the learned Vidura and the bard Saṃjaya, and likewise that great archer Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat.

sanskrit: sa praviśya gṛhaṃ rājā kṛtapūrvāhṇikakriyaḥ tarpayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhān āhāram akarot tadā
english: Having entered his house and performed the morning rites, the king satisfied the foremost of the twice-born and then took his meal.

sanskrit: gāndhārī caiva dharmajñā kuntyā saha manasvinī vadhūbhir upacāreṇa pūjitābhuṅkta bhārata
english: And Gāndhārī, knower of dharma and high of mind, together with Kuntī, honored with attentive service by the daughters-in-law, also ate, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṛtāhāraṃ kṛtāhārāḥ sarve te vidurādayaḥ pāṇḍavāś ca kuruśreṣṭham upātiṣṭhanta taṃ nṛpam
english: When the meal was done, all of them — Vidura and the rest, and the Pāṇḍavas as well — having eaten, attended upon that king, the best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahārāja kuntīputram upahvare niṣaṇṇaṃ pāṇinā pṛṣṭhe saṃspṛśann ambikāsutaḥ
english: Then, O great king, the son of Ambikā spoke to Kuntī's son seated near at hand, touching his back with his hand.

sanskrit: apramādas tvayā kāryaḥ sarvathā kurunandana aṣṭāṅge rājaśārdūla rājye dharmapuraskṛte
english: "You must be ever vigilant, O joy of the Kurus, in every way, O tiger among kings, over the kingdom of eight limbs, with dharma set foremost."

sanskrit: tat tu śakyaṃ yathā tāta rakṣituṃ pāṇḍunandana rājyaṃ dharmaṃ ca kaunteya vidvān asi nibodha tat
english: "How the kingdom and dharma may be guarded, dear son of Pāṇḍu, O son of Kuntī — learned though you are, hear this from me."

sanskrit: vidyāvṛddhān sadaiva tvam upāsīthā yudhiṣṭhira śṛṇuyās te ca yad brūyuḥ kuryāś caivāvicārayan
english: "Wait ever upon those ripe in learning, Yudhiṣṭhira; listen to what they say, and act on it without hesitation."

sanskrit: prātar utthāya tān rājan pūjayitvā yathāvidhi kṛtyakāle samutpanne pṛcchethāḥ kāryam ātmanaḥ
english: "Rising at dawn, O king, and honoring them in due form, when the time for action comes you should ask them about your own affairs."

sanskrit: te tu saṃmānitā rājaṃs tvayā rājyahitārthinā pravakṣyanti hitaṃ tāta sarvaṃ kauravanandana
english: "Honored by you who seek the kingdom's good, O king, they will tell you all that is beneficial, dear joy of the Kurus."

sanskrit: indriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi vājivat paripālaya hitāya vai bhaviṣyanti rakṣitaṃ draviṇaṃ yathā
english: "And guard all your senses as one guards horses; rightly kept, they will turn to your good, even as wealth that is well guarded."

sanskrit: amātyān upadhātītān pitṛpaitāmahāñ śucīn dāntān karmasu sarveṣu mukhyān mukhyeṣu yojayeḥ
english: "Ministers proven beyond temptation, serving since your fathers' and grandfathers' days, pure and self-controlled — appoint the chief of them to the chief of all your tasks."

sanskrit: cārayethāś ca satataṃ cārair aviditaiḥ parān parīkṣitair bahuvidhaṃ svarāṣṭreṣu pareṣu ca
english: "And keep your foes ever under watch through spies unknown to them and well tested, in manifold fashion, both in your own realm and in others'."

sanskrit: puraṃ ca te suguptaṃ syād dṛḍhaprākāratoraṇam aṭṭāṭṭālakasaṃbādhaṃ ṣaṭpathaṃ sarvatodiśam
english: "Let your city be well defended, with stout ramparts and gateways, thick-set with watchtowers, opening on six roads to every quarter."

sanskrit: tasya dvārāṇi kāryāṇi paryāptāni bṛhanti ca sarvataḥ suvibhaktāni yantrair ārakṣitāni ca
english: "Its gates should be made ample and broad, well disposed on every side and guarded by engines of war."

sanskrit: puruṣair alam arthajñair viditaiḥ kulaśīlataḥ ātmā ca rakṣyaḥ satataṃ bhojanādiṣu bhārata
english: "By men who understand their charge, known for their family and character; and your own person too must ever be guarded, in eating and the rest, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: vihārāhārakāleṣu mālyaśayyāsaneṣu ca striyaś ca te suguptāḥ syur vṛddhair āptair adhiṣṭhitāḥ śīlavadbhiḥ kulīnaiś ca vidvadbhiś ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: "At times of pastime and of food, in garlands, bed, and seats; and let your women be well protected, set under elders trustworthy, virtuous, well-born, and wise, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: mantriṇaś caiva kurvīthā dvijān vidyāviśāradān vinītāṃś ca kulīnāṃś ca dharmārthakuśalān ṛjūn
english: "For counselors take twice-born men skilled in learning, well-disciplined and well-born, adept in dharma and artha, and upright."

sanskrit: taiḥ sārdhaṃ mantrayethās tvaṃ nātyarthaṃ bahubhiḥ saha samastair api ca vyastair vyapadeśena kena cit
english: "With them you should take counsel — but not with too many together, sometimes with all, sometimes with each apart, under some pretext or other."

sanskrit: susaṃvṛtaṃ mantragṛhaṃ sthalaṃ cāruhya mantrayeḥ araṇye niḥśalāke vā na ca rātrau kathaṃ cana
english: "Take counsel in a well-enclosed council chamber, or having climbed to high ground, or in a forest free of reeds — but never by night, in any wise."

sanskrit: vānarāḥ pakṣiṇaś caiva ye manuṣyānukāriṇaḥ sarve mantragṛhe varjyā ye cāpi jaḍapaṅgukāḥ
english: "Monkeys and birds that mimic men, and all who are dull-witted or crippled, are to be barred from the council chamber."

sanskrit: mantrabhede hi ye doṣā bhavanti pṛthivīkṣitām na te śakyāḥ samādhātuṃ kathaṃ cid iti me matiḥ
english: "For the ills that befall lords of the earth when counsel is betrayed can in no way be set right again — such is my conviction."

sanskrit: doṣāṃś ca mantrabhedeṣu brūyās tvaṃ mantrimaṇḍale abhede ca guṇān rājan punaḥ punar ariṃdama
english: "And in the circle of counselors you should declare the harms of betraying counsel, and the merits of keeping it, again and again, O king, subduer of foes."

sanskrit: paurajānapadānāṃ ca śaucāśaucaṃ yudhiṣṭhira yathā syād viditaṃ rājaṃs tathā kāryam ariṃdama
english: "And the honesty and dishonesty of townsmen and countryfolk, Yudhiṣṭhira — see that it becomes known to you, O king, and act accordingly, subduer of foes."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca vyavahārāś ca te tāta nityam āptair adhiṣṭhitāḥ yojyās tuṣṭair hitai rājan nityaṃ cārair anuṣṭhitāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "And your legal affairs, dear son, should ever be set under trustworthy men — men contented and devoted, O king — and constantly watched over by spies."

sanskrit: parimāṇaṃ viditvā ca daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu bhārata praṇayeyur yathānyāyaṃ puruṣās te yudhiṣṭhira
english: "Knowing the due measure, O Bhārata, your men should impose punishment upon the punishable according to law, Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: ādānarucayaś caiva paradārābhimarśakāḥ ugradaṇḍapradhānāś ca mithyā vyāhāriṇas tathā
english: "Those given to plunder, violators of others' wives, those foremost in cruel oppression, and speakers of falsehood;"

sanskrit: ākroṣṭāraś ca lubdhāś ca hantāraḥ sāhasapriyāḥ sabhāvihārabhettāro varṇānāṃ ca pradūṣakāḥ hiraṇyadaṇḍyā vadhyāś ca kartavyā deśakālataḥ
english: "revilers and the greedy, murderers fond of reckless deeds, breakers of assembly and pastime, and corrupters of the social orders — these are to be fined in gold or put to death, according to place and time."

sanskrit: prātar eva hi paśyethā ye kuryur vyayakarma te alaṃkāram atho bhojyam ata ūrdhvaṃ samācareḥ
english: "At dawn you should review those who manage expenditure; thereafter attend to your adornment and your food."

sanskrit: paśyethāś ca tato yodhān sadā tvaṃ pariharṣayan dūtānāṃ ca carāṇāṃ ca pradoṣas te sadā bhavet
english: "Then you should review your warriors, ever cheering them on; and for envoys and spies let the early evening always be your time."

sanskrit: sadā cāpararātraṃ te bhavet kāryārthanirṇaye madhyarātre vihāras te madhyāhne ca sadā bhavet
english: "Let the last watch of the night always be yours for settling the business of state; at midnight your repose, and at midday too your rest."

sanskrit: sarve tv ātyayikāḥ kālāḥ kāryāṇāṃ bharatarṣabha tathaivālaṃkṛtaḥ kāle tiṣṭhethā bhūridakṣiṇaḥ cakravat karmaṇāṃ tāta paryāyo hy eṣa nityaśaḥ
english: "Yet all hours are urgent when affairs press, O bull of the Bharatas; so, adorned and lavish in gifts, hold yourself ready at the proper time — for the round of duties, dear son, turns ceaselessly like a wheel."

sanskrit: kośasya saṃcaye yatnaṃ kurvīthā nyāyataḥ sadā dvividhasya mahārāja viparītaṃ vivarjayeḥ
english: "Make effort always, by lawful means, to gather your treasury of both kinds, O great king, and shun whatever is contrary to law."

sanskrit: cārair viditvā śatrūṃś ca ye te rājyāntarāyiṇaḥ tān āptaiḥ puruṣair dūrād ghātayethāḥ parasparam
english: "Learning through spies of those enemies who would obstruct your rule, you should have them slain from afar by trusty men, one against another."

sanskrit: karmadṛṣṭyātha bhṛtyāṃs tvaṃ varayethāḥ kurūdvaha kārayethāś ca karmāṇi yuktāyuktair adhiṣṭhitaiḥ
english: "Then, judging by their work, choose your servants, O scion of the Kurus, and have tasks carried out under men suited and unsuited each to their place."

sanskrit: senāpraṇetā ca bhavet tava tāta dṛḍhavrataḥ śūraḥ kleśasahaś caiva priyaś ca tava mānavaḥ
english: "And let the leader of your army, dear son, be a man firm in his vows, brave, enduring of hardship, and dear to you."

sanskrit: sarve jānapadāś caiva tava karmāṇi pāṇḍava paurogavāś ca sabhyāś ca kuryur ye vyavahāriṇaḥ
english: "And let all your country-officers, O Pāṇḍava, your stewards and assessors, attend to your affairs — they who conduct the dealings of state."

sanskrit: svarandhraṃ pararandhraṃ ca sveṣu caiva pareṣu ca upalakṣayitavyaṃ te nityam eva yudhiṣṭhira
english: "Your own weak points and the enemy's, among your own people and among others' — these you must mark always, Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: deśāntarasthāś ca narā vikrāntāḥ sarvakarmasu mātrābhir anurūpābhir anugrāhyā hitās tvayā
english: "And men dwelling in other lands, valiant in every kind of work, should be won over by you with fitting favors, to your benefit."

sanskrit: guṇārthināṃ guṇaḥ kāryo viduṣāṃ te janādhipa avicālyāś ca te te syur yathā merur mahāgiriḥ
english: "Esteem must be shown to those learned men who prize merit, O lord of men; and let each of them stand unshakable as the great mountain Meru."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca maṇḍalāni ca budhyethāḥ pareṣām ātmanas tathā udāsīnaguṇānāṃ ca madhyamānāṃ tathaiva ca
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "And you should understand the circles of states — those of your foes, and of yourself, and likewise of the neutrals and of the middle powers."

sanskrit: caturṇāṃ śatrujātānāṃ sarveṣām ātatāyinām mitraṃ cāmitramitraṃ ca boddhavyaṃ te 'rikarśana
english: "Of the four kinds of enemies, all of them aggressors, you must discern friend and the friend of an enemy, O harrier of foes."

sanskrit: tathāmātyā janapadā durgāṇi viṣamāṇi ca balāni ca kuruśreṣṭha bhavanty eṣāṃ yathecchakam
english: "And ministers, territories, fortresses, difficult terrain, and armies, O best of the Kurus, belong to these powers at their pleasure."

sanskrit: te ca dvādaśa kaunteya rājñāṃ vai vividhātmakāḥ mantripradhānāś ca guṇāḥ ṣaṣṭir dvādaśa ca prabho
english: "These powers of kings, O son of Kuntī, are twelve, of varied nature; and the constituents headed by the ministers are sixty and twelve, O lord."

sanskrit: etan maṇḍalam ity āhur ācāryā nītikovidāḥ atra ṣāḍguṇyam āyattaṃ yudhiṣṭhira nibodha tat
english: "This the masters skilled in statecraft call the circle of states; upon it rest the six measures of policy, Yudhiṣṭhira — learn that."

sanskrit: vṛddhikṣayau ca vijñeyau sthānaṃ ca kurunandana dvisaptatyā mahābāho tataḥ ṣāḍguṇyacāriṇaḥ
english: "Increase and decline, and stability too, must be discerned, O joy of the Kurus; by these seventy-two, mighty-armed one, follow then the six measures of policy."

sanskrit: yadā svapakṣo balavān parapakṣas tathābalaḥ vigṛhya śatrūn kaunteya yāyāt kṣitipatis tadā yadā svapakṣo 'balavāṃs tadā saṃdhiṃ samāśrayet
english: "When one's own side is strong and the enemy's side weak, then, having made open war upon his foes, the lord of earth should march, O son of Kuntī; but when one's own side is weak, then he should resort to peace."

sanskrit: dravyāṇāṃ saṃcayaś caiva kartavyaḥ syān mahāṃs tathā yadā samartho yānāya nacireṇaiva bhārata
english: "And a great store of goods should likewise be amassed, so that one becomes fit to march out before long, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: tadā sarvaṃ vidheyaṃ syāt sthānaṃ ca na vibhājayet bhūmir alpaphalā deyā viparītasya bhārata
english: "Then let all be made ready, and let him not partition his ground; land of little yield may be ceded to one in the opposite case, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: hiraṇyaṃ kupyabhūyiṣṭhaṃ mitraṃ kṣīṇam akośavat viparītān na gṛhṇīyāt svayaṃ saṃdhiviśāradaḥ
english: "Gold abounding in base metal, an ally enfeebled and without a treasury — such inferior things one skilled in treaties should not himself accept."

sanskrit: saṃdhyarthaṃ rājaputraṃ ca lipsethā bharatarṣabha viparītas tu te 'deyaḥ putra kasyāṃ cid āpadi tasya pramokṣe yatnaṃ ca kuryāḥ sopāyamantravit
english: "For the sake of a treaty you may seek to obtain a prince, O bull of the Bharatas; but in any emergency you should not surrender your own son in turn — rather, knowing the means and counsels, strive for his release."

sanskrit: prakṛtīnāṃ ca kaunteya rājā dīnāṃ vibhāvayet krameṇa yugapad dvaṃdvaṃ vyasanānāṃ balābalam
english: "And a king should weigh the strength and weakness of his afflicted subjects' calamities, O son of Kuntī — in turn, all at once, or two by two."

sanskrit: pīḍanaṃ stambhanaṃ caiva kośabhaṅgas tathaiva ca kāryaṃ yatnena śatrūṇāṃ svarāṣṭraṃ rakṣatā svayam
english: "The harassing, the crippling, and the breaking of the treasury of his foes should be wrought with effort by one who himself guards his own realm."

sanskrit: na ca hiṃsyo 'bhyupagataḥ sāmanto vṛddhim icchatā kaunteya taṃ na hiṃseta yo mahīṃ vijigīṣate
english: "A neighboring lord who has submitted should not be harmed by one who desires increase, O son of Kuntī; he who seeks to conquer the earth should do him no injury."

sanskrit: gaṇānāṃ bhedane yogaṃ gacchethāḥ saha mantribhiḥ sādhusaṃgrahaṇāc caiva pāpanigrahaṇāt tathā
english: "You should, with your counselors, contrive the dividing of confederacies — likewise by gathering the good to you and by restraining the wicked."

sanskrit: durbalāś cāpi satataṃ nāvaṣṭabhyā balīyasā tiṣṭhethā rājaśārdūla vaitasīṃ vṛttim āsthitaḥ
english: "And the weak should never be oppressed unceasingly by the stronger; stand firm, O tiger among kings, adopting the way of the reed."

sanskrit: yady evam abhiyāyāc ca durbalaṃ balavān nṛpaḥ sāmādibhir upāyais taṃ krameṇa vinivartayet
english: "And if a mighty king should thus march against the weak, the latter should turn him back step by step by the expedients beginning with conciliation."

sanskrit: aśaknuvaṃs tu yuddhāya niṣpatet saha mantribhiḥ kośena paurair daṇḍena ye cānye priyakāriṇaḥ
english: "But if unable to give battle, let him sally forth together with his counselors, his treasury, his townsfolk, his army, and whatever others wish him well."

sanskrit: asaṃbhave tu sarvasya yathāmukhyena niṣpatet krameṇānena mokṣaḥ syāc charīram api kevalam
english: "And if all this be impossible, let him escape with what is most precious; by this gradual course deliverance may be had — even of the bare body alone."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca saṃdhivigraham apy atra paśyethā rājasattama dviyoniṃ trividhopāyaṃ bahukalpaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Herein too you should regard peace and war, O best of kings — twofold in origin, threefold in means, and of many forms, Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: rājendra paryupāsīthāś chittvā dvaividhyam ātmanaḥ tuṣṭapuṣṭabalaḥ śatrur ātmavān iti ca smaret
english: "O lord of kings, having resolved your own duality, you should bide your time; and remember that the enemy too is self-possessed, with contented and well-nourished forces."

sanskrit: paryupāsanakāle tu viparītaṃ vidhīyate āmardakāle rājendra vyapasarpas tato varaḥ
english: "At a time for biding, the opposite is enjoined; at a time of crushing assault, O lord of kings, withdrawal is then the better course."

sanskrit: vyasanaṃ bhedanaṃ caiva śatrūṇāṃ kārayet tataḥ karśanaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ caiva yuddhe cāpi bahukṣayam
english: "He should then bring upon his foes calamity and division, wasting and terror, and in battle too great destruction."

sanskrit: prayāsyamāno nṛpatis trividhaṃ paricintayet ātmanaś caiva śatroś ca śaktiṃ śāstraviśāradaḥ
english: "A king about to march, well versed in the treatises, should ponder threefold the power both of himself and of his foe."

sanskrit: utsāhaprabhuśaktibhyāṃ mantraśaktyā ca bhārata upapanno naro yāyād viparītam ato 'nyathā
english: "Furnished with the power of energy, the power of sovereignty, and the power of counsel, O Bhārata, a man may march; otherwise, the opposite."

sanskrit: ādadīta balaṃ rājā maulaṃ mitrabalaṃ tathā aṭavībalaṃ bhṛtaṃ caiva tathā śreṇībalaṃ ca yat
english: "A king should muster his hereditary force, the force of allies, the force of forest tribes, the hired force, and whatever force of the guilds there is."

sanskrit: tatra mitrabalaṃ rājan maulena na viśiṣyate śreṇībalaṃ bhṛtaṃ caiva tulya eveti me matiḥ
english: "Of these, O king, the force of allies is not superior to the hereditary force; and the force of guilds and the hired force are equal — such is my view."

sanskrit: tathā cārabalaṃ caiva parasparasamaṃ nṛpa vijñeyaṃ balakāleṣu rājñā kāla upasthite
english: "Likewise the force of forest tribes is to be reckoned equal to these, O king, by a ruler in times of mustering, when the hour is at hand."

sanskrit: āpadaś cāpi boddhavyā bahurūpā narādhipa bhavanti rājñāṃ kauravya yās tāḥ pṛthag ataḥ śṛṇu
english: "And the calamities of many forms that befall kings must also be understood, O lord of men, O Kaurava — hear of them now severally."

sanskrit: vikalpā bahavo rājann āpadāṃ pāṇḍunandana sāmādibhir upanyasya śamayet tān nṛpaḥ sadā
english: "Many are the varieties of calamities, O king, joy of the Pāṇḍus; by employing conciliation and the rest, a king should ever quell them."

sanskrit: yātrāṃ yāyād balair yukto rājā ṣaḍbhiḥ paraṃtapa saṃyukto deśakālābhyāṃ balair ātmaguṇais tathā
english: "A king should set out on his march furnished with the six forces, O scorcher of foes, joined with the right place and time, with his troops and his own virtues."

sanskrit: tuṣṭapuṣṭabalo yāyād rājā vṛddhyudaye rataḥ āhūtaś cāpy atho yāyād anṛtāv api pārthivaḥ
english: "With contented and well-nourished forces a king bent on rising prosperity should march; and when summoned, a ruler should march even out of season."

sanskrit: sthūṇāśmānaṃ vājirathapradhānāṃ; dhvajadrumaiḥ saṃvṛtakūlarodhasam padātināgair bahukardamāṃ nadīṃ; sapatnanāśe nṛpatiḥ prayāyāt
english: "For the ruin of his rivals a king should march forth like one crossing a river whose stones are the pillars, whose chief current is horses and chariots, whose banks and bluffs are screened by tree-like banners, made miry by foot-soldiers and elephants."

sanskrit: athopapattyā śakaṭaṃ padmaṃ vajraṃ ca bhārata uśanā veda yac chāstraṃ tatraitad vihitaṃ vibho
english: "Then, as occasion fits, the cart array, the lotus, and the thunderbolt array, O Bhārata — the science that Uśanas knows, therein all this is ordained, O lord."

sanskrit: sādayitvā parabalaṃ kṛtvā ca balaharṣaṇam svabhūmau yojayed yuddhaṃ parabhūmau tathaiva ca
english: "Having crushed the enemy's force and roused the ardor of his own, he should join battle on his own ground and likewise on the enemy's."

sanskrit: labdhaṃ praśamayed rājā nikṣiped dhanino narān jñātvā svaviṣayaṃ taṃ ca sāmādibhir upakramet
english: "What he has won the king should pacify, and settle wealthy men there; and recognizing that land as his own domain, he should approach it with conciliation and the rest."
